sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu tān vṛkṣān paśyamāno nagottame bhīmasenam idaṃ vākyam abravīn madhurākṣaram
english: While Yudhiṣṭhira was gazing upon those trees on that best of mountains, he spoke these sweet-syllabled words to Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: paśya bhīma śubhān deśān devākrīḍān samantataḥ amānuṣagatiṃ prāptāḥ saṃsiddhāḥ sma vṛkodara
english: "Behold, Bhīma, these auspicious regions on all sides — the playgrounds of the gods. We have attained a course beyond mortal reach and have truly accomplished our purpose, O Wolf-belly."

sanskrit: latābhiś caiva bahvībhiḥ puṣpitāḥ pādapottamāḥ saṃśliṣṭāḥ pārtha śobhante gandhamādanasānuṣu
english: The finest trees, covered with blossoms and embraced by many creepers, shine on the slopes of Gandhamādana, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinībhiś caratāṃ sahitānāṃ śikhaṇḍinām nardatāṃ śṛṇu nirghoṣaṃ bhīma parvatasānuṣu
english: Hear, O Bhīma, the resounding calls of peacocks sporting together with their hens, crying out on the mountain slopes.

sanskrit: cakorāḥ śatapatrāś ca mattakokilaśārikāḥ patriṇaḥ puṣpitān etān saṃśliṣyanti mahādrumān
english: Chakora partridges, red-legged partridges, intoxicated cuckoos, and mynahs — these birds cling to these blooming great trees.

sanskrit: raktapītāruṇāḥ pārtha pādapāgragatā dvijāḥ parasparam udīkṣante bahavo jīvajīvakāḥ
english: Red, yellow, and ruddy — perched atop the trees, O Pārtha — many chakravaka birds gaze upon one another.

sanskrit: haritāruṇavarṇānāṃ śādvalānāṃ samantataḥ sārasāḥ pratidṛśyante śailaprasravaṇeṣv api
english: Cranes are seen everywhere among the green and reddish-hued meadows, and also at the mountain springs.

sanskrit: vadanti madhurā vācaḥ sarvabhūtamanonugāḥ bhṛṅgarājopacakrāś ca lohapṛṣṭhāś ca patriṇaḥ
english: Sweet voices pleasing to all creatures are uttered by the king-bees, the chakravaka ducks, and the red-backed birds.

sanskrit: caturviṣāṇāḥ padmābhāḥ kuñjarāḥ sakareṇavaḥ ete vaiḍūryavarṇābhaṃ kṣobhayanti mahat saraḥ
english: Four-tusked, lotus-hued elephants with their she-elephants are stirring this great lake that gleams like lapis lazuli.

sanskrit: bahutālasamutsedhāḥ śailaśṛṅgāt paricyutāḥ nānāprasravaṇebhyaś ca vāridhārāḥ patanty amūḥ
english: Streams of water fall from many springs and from the mountain peaks, as tall as many palm trees in height.

sanskrit: bhāskarābhaprabhā bhīma śāradābhraghanopamāḥ śobhayanti mahāśailaṃ nānārajatadhātavaḥ
english: Radiant as the sun, resembling thick autumnal clouds, the various silver-hued mineral ores adorn this great mountain, O Bhīma.

sanskrit: kva cid añjanavarṇābhāḥ kva cit kāñcanasaṃnibhāḥ dhātavo haritālasya kva cid dhiṅgulakasya ca
english: In some places the mineral veins are collyrium-dark, in others they resemble gold; in some places are deposits of orpiment, and in others of red arsenic.

sanskrit: manaḥśilāguhāś caiva saṃdhyābhranikaropamāḥ śaśalohitavarṇābhāḥ kva cid gairikadhātavaḥ
english: There are realgar-veined caves resembling twilight clouds, and in some places ochre-red mineral deposits the color of red lac.

sanskrit: sitāsitābhrapratimā bālasūryasamaprabhāḥ ete bahuvidhāḥ śailaṃ śobhayanti mahāprabhāḥ
english: Resembling white and dark clouds, glowing like the morning sun — these manifold and brilliantly luminous minerals adorn the mountain.

sanskrit: gandharvāḥ saha kāntābhir yathoktaṃ vṛṣaparvaṇā dṛśyante śailaśṛṅgeṣu pārtha kiṃpuruṣaiḥ saha
english: Gandharvas with their beloved consorts, as described by Vṛṣaparvan, are seen on the mountain peaks together with the kinnaras, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: gītānāṃ talatālānāṃ yathā sāmnāṃ ca nisvanaḥ śrūyate bahudhā bhīma sarvabhūtamanoharaḥ
english: The sounds of songs, hand-clapping, and samans are heard in many ways here, O Bhīma, enchanting the hearts of all beings.

sanskrit: mahāgaṅgām udīkṣasva puṇyāṃ devanadīṃ śubhām kalahaṃsagaṇair juṣṭām ṛṣikiṃnarasevitām
english: Behold the great Gaṅgā, the sacred and auspicious river of the gods, frequented by flocks of bar-headed geese, and attended by sages and kinnaras.

sanskrit: dhātubhiś ca saridbhiś ca kiṃnarair mṛgapakṣibhiḥ gandharvair apsarobhiś ca kānanaiś ca manoramaiḥ
english: With its mineral streaks and streams, kinnaras, deer and birds, gandharvas and apsaras, and its enchanting groves —

sanskrit: vyālaiś ca vividhākāraiḥ śataśīrṣaiḥ samantataḥ upetaṃ paśya kaunteya śailarājam ariṃdama
english: — and with serpents of various forms and hundred-headed snakes all around, behold the king of mountains, O son of Kuntī, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: te prītamanasaḥ śūrāḥ prāptā gatim anuttamām nātṛpyan parvatendrasya darśanena paraṃtapāḥ
english: Those heroes, joyful in heart, having attained the highest course, were not satiated with beholding the king of mountains, those scorchers of enemies.

sanskrit: upetam atha mālyaiś ca phalavadbhiś ca pādapaiḥ ārṣṭiṣeṇasya rājarṣer āśramaṃ dadṛśus tadā
english: Then they saw the hermitage of the royal sage Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, adorned with garlands and fruit-bearing trees.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ tīvratapasaṃ kṛśaṃ dhamanisaṃtatam pāragaṃ sarvadharmāṇām ārṣṭiṣeṇam upāgaman
english: Then they approached Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, that intense ascetic, lean and with prominent veins, who had traversed to the further shore of all dharmas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yudhiṣṭhiras tam āsādya tapasā dagdhakilbiṣam abhyavādayata prītaḥ śirasā nāma kīrtayan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Yudhiṣṭhira, approaching that one whose sins had been burned away by austerity, greeted him joyfully, bowing his head and pronouncing his name.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇā ca bhīmaś ca yamau cāpi yaśasvinau śirobhiḥ prāpya rājarṣiṃ parivāryopatasthire
english: Then Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī) and Bhīma and the glorious twins also came forward, bowing their heads to the royal sage, surrounding and standing near him.

sanskrit: tathaiva dhaumyo dharmajñaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ purohitaḥ yathānyāyam upākrāntas tam ṛṣiṃ saṃśitavratam
english: Likewise Dhaumya, knower of dharma, the family priest of the Pāṇḍavas, approached that sage of sharpened vows in due and proper manner.

sanskrit: anvajānāt sa dharmajño munir divyena cakṣuṣā pāṇḍoḥ putrān kuruśreṣṭhān āsyatām iti cābravīt
english: That wise sage, with his divine sight, recognized them as the sons of Pāṇḍu, the best of Kurus, and said to them: "Be seated."

sanskrit: kurūṇām ṛṣabhaṃ prājñaṃ pūjayitvā mahātapāḥ saha bhrātṛbhir āsīnaṃ paryapṛcchad anāmayam
english: After honoring the wise bull of the Kurus, the great ascetic inquired after his well-being as he sat with his brothers.

sanskrit: nānṛte kuruṣe bhāvaṃ kaccid dharme ca vartase matāpitroś ca te vṛttiḥ kaccit pārtha na sīdati
english: "Do you not incline toward falsehood? Do you conduct yourself in dharma? Does your conduct toward your mother and father not falter, O Pārtha?"

sanskrit: kaccit te guravaḥ sarve vṛddhā vaidyāś ca pūjitāḥ kaccin na kuruṣe bhāvaṃ pārtha pāpeṣu karmasu
english: "Are all your elders, the aged, and the learned properly honored? Do you not incline toward sinful acts, O Pārtha?"

sanskrit: sukṛtaṃ pratikartuṃ ca kaccid dhātuṃ ca duṣkṛtam yathānyāyaṃ kuruśreṣṭha jānāsi na ca katthase
english: "Do you know, O best of Kurus, how to repay good deeds and to restrain evil deeds in due and proper measure, and do you not boast of it?"

sanskrit: yathārhaṃ mānitāḥ kaccit tvayā nandanti sādhavaḥ vaneṣv api vasan kaccid dharmam evānuvartase
english: "Do the virtuous rejoice, honored by you as they deserve? Even dwelling in the forests, do you follow dharma alone?"

sanskrit: kaccid dhaumyas tvadācārair na pārtha paritapyate dānadharmatapaḥśaucair ārjavena titikṣayā
english: "Is Dhaumya not distressed by your conduct, O Pārtha — by your charity, dharma, austerity, purity, uprightness, and forbearance?"

sanskrit: pitṛpaitāmahaṃ vṛttaṃ kaccit pārthānuvartase kaccid rājarṣiyātena pathā gacchasi pāṇḍava
english: "Do you follow the conduct of your fathers and grandfathers, O Pārtha? Do you walk the path trodden by the royal sages, O son of Pāṇḍu?"

sanskrit: sve sve kila kule jāte putre naptari vā punaḥ pitaraḥ pitṛlokasthāḥ śocanti ca hasanti ca
english: "It is said that the fathers dwelling in the world of the ancestors grieve and rejoice over each son or grandson born in their own respective lineage."

sanskrit: kiṃ nv asya duṣkṛte 'smābhiḥ saṃprāptavyaṃ bhaviṣyati kiṃ cāsya sukṛte 'smābhiḥ prāptavyam iti śobhanam
english: "'What shall we receive through his evil deeds?' they wonder, and 'What auspicious good shall we obtain through his meritorious deeds?'"

sanskrit: pitā mātā tathaivāgnir gurur ātmā ca pañcamaḥ yasyaite pūjitāḥ pārtha tasya lokāv ubhau jitau
english: "Father, mother, fire, teacher, and the self as the fifth — whoever honors these, O Pārtha, has conquered both worlds."

sanskrit: abbhakṣā vāyubhakṣāś ca plavamānā vihāyasā juṣante parvataśreṣṭham ṛṣayaḥ parvasaṃdhiṣu
english: "Sages who subsist on water and on air, floating through the sky, frequent this best of mountains at the junctions of the fortnights."

sanskrit: kāminaḥ saha kāntābhiḥ parasparam anuvratāḥ dṛśyante śailaśṛṅgasthās tathā kiṃpuruṣā nṛpa
english: "Kinnaras who are devoted to their loves, faithful to one another, are seen standing on the mountain peaks, O king."

sanskrit: arajāṃsi ca vāsāṃsi vasānāḥ kauśikāni ca dṛśyante bahavaḥ pārtha gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ
english: "Wearing dustless garments of silk, many hosts of gandharvas and apsaras are seen here, O Pārtha."

sanskrit: vidyādharagaṇāś caiva sragviṇaḥ priyadarśanāḥ mahoragagaṇāś caiva suparṇāś coragādayaḥ
english: "Troops of vidyadharas, garlanded and fair to behold, and companies of great serpents, and garudas and nagas and the like —"

sanskrit: asya copari śailasya śrūyate parvasaṃdhiṣu bherīpaṇavaśaṅkhānāṃ mṛdaṅgānāṃ ca nisvanaḥ
english: "— and above this mountain, at the junction of the fortnights, the sounds of kettledrums, small drums, conches, and mridangas are heard."

sanskrit: ihasthair eva tat sarvaṃ śrotavyaṃ bharatarṣabhāḥ na kāryā vaḥ kathaṃ cit syāt tatrābhisaraṇe matiḥ
english: "All of this is to be heard from right here, O bulls of the Bhārata line — under no circumstances should you entertain any thought of going there."

sanskrit: na cāpy ataḥ paraṃ śakyaṃ gantuṃ bharatasattamāḥ vihāro hy atra devānām amānuṣagatis tu sā
english: "Nor is it possible to go beyond this point, O best of Bhāratas — that is the sport-realm of the gods, a course beyond mortal reach."

sanskrit: īṣaccapalakarmāṇaṃ manuṣyam iha bhārata dviṣanti sarvabhūtāni tāḍayanti ca rākṣasāḥ
english: "All beings here hate a man who acts even slightly rashly, O Bhārata, and the rakshasas will beat him."

sanskrit: abhyatikramya śikharaṃ śailasyāsya yudhiṣṭhira gatiḥ paramasiddhānāṃ devarṣīṇāṃ prakāśate
english: "Beyond the summit of this mountain, O Yudhiṣṭhira, lies the path of the highest perfected beings and the divine sages."

sanskrit: cāpalād iha gacchantaṃ pārtha yānam ataḥ param ayaḥśūlādibhir ghnanti rākṣasāḥ śatrusūdana
english: "One who proceeds rashly to that further realm, O Pārtha, O slayer of foes, is struck down by rakshasas with iron spears and other weapons."

sanskrit: apsarobhiḥ parivṛtaḥ samṛddhyā naravāhanaḥ iha vaiśravaṇas tāta parvasaṃdhiṣu dṛśyate
english: "Surrounded by apsaras and in full splendor, Vaiśravaṇa the lord who is carried by men is seen here at the junctions of the fortnights, my dear."

sanskrit: śikhare taṃ samāsīnam adhipaṃ sarvarakṣasām prekṣante sarvabhūtāni bhānumantam ivoditam
english: "All beings behold him seated on the peak, the lord of all rakshasas, like the sun risen in its splendor."

sanskrit: devadānavasiddhānāṃ tathā vaiśravaṇasya ca gireḥ śikharaṃ udyānam idaṃ bharatasattama
english: "This mountain summit is the garden of the gods, the danavas, the siddhas, and of Vaiśravaṇa himself, O best of the Bhāratas."

sanskrit: upāsīnasya dhanadaṃ tumburoḥ parvasaṃdhiṣu gītasāmasvanas tāta śrūyate gandhamādane
english: "While Tumburu waits upon the wealth-giver, the sounds of his song-samans are heard here on Gandhamādana at the junctions of the fortnights, my dear."

sanskrit: etad evaṃvidhaṃ citram iha tāta yudhiṣṭhira prekṣante sarvabhūtāni bahuśaḥ parvasaṃdhiṣu
english: "Such marvelous things as these are witnessed here, my dear Yudhiṣṭhira, by all beings, many times at the junctions of the fortnights."

sanskrit: bhuñjānāḥ sarvabhojyāni rasavanti phalāni ca vasadhvaṃ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭhā yāvad arjunadarśanam
english: "Eating all manner of foods and flavorful fruits, dwell here, O best of Pāṇḍavas, until the sight of Arjuna."

sanskrit: na tāta capalairbhāvyam iha prāptaiḥ kathaṃ cana uṣitveha yathākāmaṃ yathāśraddhaṃ vihṛtya ca tataḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha pṛthivīṃ pālayiṣyasi
english: "You must not be rash in any way having arrived here, my dear. Having dwelt here as long as you wish and sported as your faith dictates, you shall then, O best of weapon-bearers, protect the earth."

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca pāṇḍoḥ putrā mahātmānaḥ sarve divyaparākramāḥ kiyantaṃ kālam avasan parvate gandhamādane
english: Janamejaya said: The great-souled sons of Pāṇḍu, all of divine valor — how long did they dwell on Mount Gandhamādana?

sanskrit: kāni cābhyavahāryāṇi tatra teṣāṃ mahātmanām vasatāṃ lokavīrāṇām āsaṃs tad brūhi sattama
english: And what were the foods of those great-souled heroes of the world while they dwelt there? Tell me that, O best one.

sanskrit: vistareṇa ca me śaṃsa bhīmasenaparākramam yad yac cakre mahābāhus tasmin haimavate girau na khalv āsīt punar yuddhaṃ tasya yakṣair dvijottama
english: Tell me in detail of Bhīmasena's feats — whatever the mighty-armed one did on that Himālayan mountain. Surely there was no further battle with the yakshas, O best of the twice-born?

sanskrit: kaccit samāgamas teṣām āsīd vaiśravaṇena ca tatra hy āyāti dhanada ārṣṭiṣeṇo yathābravīt
english: Was there a meeting of theirs with Vaiśravaṇa? For the wealth-giver comes there, as Ārṣṭiṣeṇa had said.

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ vistareṇa tapodhana na hi me śṛṇvatas tṛptir asti teṣāṃ viceṣṭitam
english: This I wish to hear in detail, O storehouse of austerity — for there is no satiation in me as I listen to their deeds.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etad ātmahitaṃ śrutvā tasyāpratimatejasaḥ śāsanaṃ satataṃ cakrus tathaiva bharatarṣabhāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard this counsel that was good for their own souls from that one of incomparable splendor, the bulls of the Bhārata line constantly followed his instructions in just that way.

sanskrit: bhuñjānā munibhojyāni rasavanti phalāni ca śuddhabāṇahatānāṃ ca mṛgāṇāṃ piśitāny api
english: Eating the foods of sages, flavorful fruits, and also the flesh of deer slain by pure arrows —

sanskrit: medhyāni himavatpṛṣṭhe madhūni vividhāni ca evaṃ te nyavasaṃs tatra pāṇḍavā bharatarṣabhāḥ
english: — and the pure and various honeys on the back of the Himālaya, the Pāṇḍavas, those bulls of the Bhārata line, thus dwelt there.

sanskrit: tathā nivasatāṃ teṣāṃ pañcamaṃ varṣam abhyagāt śṛṇvatāṃ lomaśoktāni vākyāni vividhāni ca
english: As they thus dwelt there, listening to the various discourses spoken by Lomaśa, the fifth year came upon them.

sanskrit: kṛtyakāla upasthāsya iti coktvā ghaṭotkacaḥ rākṣasaiḥ sahitaḥ sarvaiḥ pūrvam eva gataḥ prabho
english: Having said "I shall come when the time of need arrives," Ghaṭotkaca departed beforehand together with all the rakshasas, O lord.

sanskrit: ārṣṭiṣeṇāśrame teṣāṃ vasatāṃ vai mahātmanām agacchan bahavo māsāḥ paśyatāṃ mahad adbhutam
english: As those great-souled ones dwelt in the hermitage of Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, many months passed as they beheld great wonders.

sanskrit: tais tatra ramamāṇaiś ca viharadbhiś ca pāṇḍavaiḥ prītimanto mahābhāgā munayaś cāraṇās tathā
english: While the Pāṇḍavas sported and wandered about there in delight, joyful and greatly blessed sages and celestial bards —

sanskrit: ājagmuḥ pāṇḍavān draṣṭuṃ siddhātmāno yatavratāḥ tais taiḥ saha kathāś cakrur divyā bharatasattamāḥ
english: — those of perfected souls and restrained vows came to behold the Pāṇḍavas, and the best of Bhāratas held divine conversations with each of them.

sanskrit: tataḥ katipayāhasya mahāhradanivāsinam ṛddhimantaṃ mahānāgaṃ suparṇaḥ sahasāharat
english: Then after a few days, a garuda suddenly seized a great and mighty serpent that dwelt in the deep lake.

sanskrit: prākampata mahāśailaḥ prāmṛdyanta mahādrumāḥ dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni pāṇḍavāś ca tad adbhutam
english: The great mountain trembled and the great trees were crushed; all beings and the Pāṇḍavas beheld that wonder.

sanskrit: tataḥ śailottamasyāgrāt pāṇḍavān prati mārutaḥ avahat sarvamālyāni gandhavanti śubhāni ca
english: Then from the summit of that best of mountains, the wind bore toward the Pāṇḍavas all manner of garlands, fragrant and auspicious.

sanskrit: tatra puṣpāṇi divyāni suhṛdbhiḥ saha pāṇḍavāḥ dadṛśuḥ pañca varṇāni draupadī ca yaśasvinī
english: There the Pāṇḍavas, together with their friends, and the glorious Draupadī beheld divine flowers of five colors.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ tataḥ kṛṣṇā kāle vacanam abravīt vivikte parvatoddeśe sukhāsīnaṃ mahābhujam
english: Then Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī) spoke timely words to Bhīmasena, who sat at ease in a secluded mountain spot, that mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: suparṇānilavegena śvasanena mahābalāt pañcavarṇāni pātyante puṣpāṇi bharatarṣabha pratyakṣaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ nadīm aśvarathāṃ prati
english: "By the mighty wind with the velocity of Garuḍa's wings, flowers of five colors are being blown, O bull of the Bhāratas, before the eyes of all beings, toward the river Ashvaratha."

sanskrit: khāṇḍave satyasaṃdhena bhrātrā tava nareśvara gandharvoragarakṣāṃsi vāsavaś ca nivāritaḥ hatā māyāvinaś cogrā dhanuḥ prāptaṃ ca gāṇḍivam
english: "In the Khāṇḍava forest, by your brother of true pledges, O lord of men, gandharvas, serpents, and rakshasas were repelled, and even Vāsava was checked; the terrible sorcerers were slain, and the Gāṇḍīva bow was obtained."

sanskrit: tavāpi sumahat tejo mahad bāhubalaṃ ca te aviṣahyam anādhṛṣyaṃ śatakratubalopamam
english: "And your own splendor is very great, and your arm-strength is immense — unbearable and unapproachable, equal to the strength of Śatakratu (Indra)."

sanskrit: tvadbāhubalavegena trāsitāḥ sarvarākṣasāḥ hitvā śailaṃ prapadyantāṃ bhīmasena diśo daśa
english: "Terrified by the force of your arm-strength, may all the rakshasas abandon the mountain and flee in the ten directions, O Bhīmasena."

sanskrit: tataḥ śailottamasyāgraṃ citramālyadharaṃ śivam vyapetabhayasaṃmohāḥ paśyantu suhṛdas tava
english: "Then, free of fear and confusion, let your friends behold the summit of that best of mountains, adorned with beautiful garlands and auspicious."

sanskrit: evaṃ praṇihitaṃ bhīma cirāt prabhṛti me manaḥ draṣṭum icchāmi śailāgraṃ tvadbāhubalam āśritā
english: "Thus is my heart fixed, O Bhīma — long have I wished to behold that mountain summit, resting on the strength of your arms."

sanskrit: tataḥ kṣiptam ivātmānaṃ draupadyā sa paraṃtapaḥ nāmṛṣyata mahābāhuḥ prahāram iva sadgavaḥ
english: Then that scorcher of foes, the mighty-armed one, could not tolerate being so urged by Draupadī, just as a good bull cannot tolerate a goad.

sanskrit: siṃharṣabhagatiḥ śrīmān udāraḥ kanakaprabhaḥ manasvī balavān dṛpto mānī śūraś ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: With the gait of a lion and a bull, glorious, noble, radiant as gold, high-spirited, strong, proud, self-respecting, and heroic — that son of Pāṇḍu —

sanskrit: lohitākṣaḥ pṛthuvyaṃso mattavāraṇavikramaḥ siṃhadaṃṣṭro bṛhatskandhaḥ śālapota ivodgataḥ
english: — red-eyed, broad-shouldered, with the might of a rutting elephant, with lion-like fangs, with massive shoulders, rising like a young sala tree —
